e:
Capnography (sustained EtCO₂ waveform) = best/gold-standard confirmation of tracheal tube placement.
CXR confirms depth, not first-line.
Head tilt–chin lift: one hand on forehead tilts head back, other lifts chin → opens airway (avoid in suspected C-spine injury).
Bupivacaine toxicity (LAST) c̅ cardiac arrest → CPR + 20% lipid emulsion (Intralipid) bolus.

LP needle path: skin → supraspinous → interspinous → ligamentum flavum → epidural space → dura → arachnoid → CSF.
Arachnoid is the last barrier before CSF.

Halothane + suxamethonium = classic triggers of malignant hyperthermia (RYR1 defect).
Non-depolarisers (D-TC, cisatracurium, rocuronium) are safe.

Head tilt–chin lift: one hand tilts head back via forehead, other lifts the chin.
Jaw thrust is done c̅ both hands at the mandibular angles.

Cefazolin = antibiotic of choice for cardiac-surgery prophylaxis (covers skin flora, Staph/Strep).
Vancomycin if MRSA/β-lactam allergy.

Recovery position = unconscious patient c̅ pulse and breathing present (protects airway, ↓es aspiration).
No pulse → CPR.
Malignant hyperthermia (volatile agent + succinylcholine): rigidity, hyperthermia, ↑ EtCO₂ → IV dantrolene (RyR1 blocker).

Atracurium releases histamine (benzylisoquinoline) → flushing, rash, hypotension.
Cisatracurium is histamine-sparing.
Needle cricothyroidotomy is only a temporary bridge (~30–45 min, hypercarbia) → must be followed by a definitive airway (formal tracheostomy).
